title: An optimized co-immunoprecipitation protocol for the analysis of endogenous protein-protein interactions in cell lines using mass spectrometry
protocol: Start with a mammalian cell line that reached confluency of around 80%.
Remove culture medium by aspiration and discard it.
Wash cells with 10 mL ice-cold PBS; discard the PBS used for washing.
Add 2 mL of ice-cold PBS to each 100 mm plate.
Detach cells from the plate using a cell scraper.
Transfer the cell suspension in PBS to a conical centrifuge tube using a pipette.
Centrifuge the sample for 10 min at 4°C at 1,000×g.
Discard the supernatant and use the cell pellet for further steps.
Lysate cells by adding an amount of lysis buffer that is 3 times the volume of the pellet (v/v).
Disrupt the cell pellet using lysis buffer.
Incubate the lysed cells on ice for 30 minutes in Eppendorf tubes.
Centrifuge the mixture at 4°C for 15 minutes at 16,000×g.
Transfer the supernatant containing soluble protein extract to a new Eppendorf tube.
Determine the protein concentration using BCA Protein Assay kit.
Aliquot samples containing 2.5 mg of protein in Eppendorf tubes and store them at -80°C.
Weigh 3 mg of Dynabeads® M-270 Epoxy beads for each sample.
Transfer the beads into a microcentrifuge tube.
Add 1 mL of C1 to the beads and slowly pipette up and down.
Place the tubes with beads inside a tube rack with magnets for 1 minute.
Remove and discard the supernatant.
Take care not to disturb the accumulated beads during supernatant removal.
Use gel loading tips for the supernatant removal to avoid accidentally removing the beads.
Remove tubes containing Dynabeads from the magnetic rack.
Add 50 μg of antibody specific for the protein of interest (bait protein) to the tube with Dynabeads.
In a separate tube, add 50 μg of normal IgG as a negative control.
Ensure the negative control uses normal IgG sourced from the same species as the Ab used for the bait protein.
Add an appropriate volume of C1 to each tube (from steps involving beads and antibodies) to reach a final volume of 150 μL.
Add 150 μL of C2 to each tube.
Incubate tubes at 37°C for approximately 18 hours on an orbital rotator.
Add 7.5 mM sterile NaOH to achieve a concentration of 1.25 mg/ml.
Ensure beads are mixed well, using a higher rotation speed for the first 30 minutes.
Incubate the mixture gently on an orbital rotator for 18 hours.
Place tubes on a magnet for 1 minute and remove supernatants carefully.
Wash the beads by adding 800 μL of solution HB and pipetting up and down at least 10 times.
Place tubes on a magnet, discard supernatant, and repeat washing steps with solutions LB and SB sequentially.
Incubate beads in 800 μL of solution SB for 15 minutes at 25°C.
Place tubes on a magnet to remove supernatants carefully.
Add 800 μL of PBS + BSA to the beads and mix gently using a rotator for 5 minutes at 25°C.
Place the tubes on a magnet for 1 minute.
Carefully remove and discard the supernatants.
Place the antibody-conjugated beads on ice and use immediately.
Incubate cell lysates containing 2.5 mg of total proteins with antibody-coupled beads at 4°C for 18–24 hours with orbital rotation.
Place the tubes on a magnet for 1 minute after incubation.
Carefully remove and discard the supernatants.
Add BW-A buffer to the beads and gently pipette up and down at least 10 times.
Place the tubes on a magnet for 1 minute and carefully remove and discard the supernatants.
Repeat steps 32 and 33 an additional 3 times.
After removing the tube from the magnet, add BW-B buffer.
Place the samples on an orbital rotator for 5 min at 25°C.
Place the tubes on a magnet for 1 min to separate supernatants and remove them carefully.
Add 500 μL of SE buffer to the beads.
Incubate the samples on an orbital rotator for 10 min at 25°C.
Check the pH of the sample with a pH strip.
Neutralize the sample with acetic acid if necessary.
Concentrate the samples using a SpeedVac to a volume around 50 μL.
Store the concentrated samples at -80°C until further use.
Confirm Co-IP success using Western blot.
Use 5 μL or less out of 50 μL of the total immunoprecipitate for the Western blot.
Check that the band corresponding to the bait protein is visible only in the immunoprecipitate from Ab-conjugated beads and not in negative IgG controls.
Prepare samples for LC-MS/MS using an in-gel digestion protocol.
Mix 40 μL of protein immunoprecipitate with 10 μL of XT Sample Buffer containing added XT Reducing Agent.
Incubate samples for 7 min at 95°C using a ThermoMixer at 800 rpm.
Load 45-50 μL of the sample on a 10% Criterion XT Bis-Tris gel.
Stop electrophoresis when the dye front moves around 2 inches from the base of the well.
Wash the gel with water after removing it from its plates.
Stain the gel with Coomassie Brilliant Blue G-250 for 2 h or use InstantBlue Stain Solution to complete staining and destaining in less than 20 min.
Destain the gel for around 18–24 h.
Cut out a 2-inch lane into 3 or more slices with a disposable scalpel.
Transfer the slices into a 1.5-mL Eppendorf tube.
Thoroughly wash the scalpel with water, then methanol, then water again between each slice excision to reduce cross-contamination.
Add 100 μL of HPLC-grade water to each tube containing a gel slice.
Agitate the tubes on the ThermoMixer for 10 min.
Remove and discard the supernatant.
Add 100 μL of ACN to the gel slices.
Incubate the tubes at room temperature for 5–10 min.
Remove and discard the supernatant.
If gel pieces are still blue, add another 100 μL of ACN and shake for an additional 15 minutes or until the blue stain is removed from the gel slice.
Make 100 μL of TCEP reduction solution by combining 10 μL of 20 mM tris(2-carboxyethyl)phosphine (TCEP) with 90 μL of 50 mM ammonium bicarbonate (AmBic).
Add 100 μL of the TCEP solution to each gel slice.
Incubate the tubes at 37°C for 30 min on the ThermoMixer.
If necessary, add 100 μL of ACN and shake for 15 min at 25°C.
Remove and discard the supernatant.
Add 100 μL of ACN to each tube.
Agitate tubes on ThermoMixer for 5 min at 25°C.
Remove and discard supernatant.
Make IAA alkylation solution by combining 10 μL of 375 mM IAA with 90 μL of 50 mM AmBic.
Add 100 μL of IAA solution to each gel slice.
Incubate samples for 20 min at 25°C in the dark.
Remove and discard supernatant.
Add 100 μL of ACN to each gel slice.
Incubate samples for 10 min.
Remove and discard supernatant.
Allow gel slices to air-dry for 10 min.
Add trypsin solution (20-50 μL) to cover gel slices.
Incubate samples on ice for 30 min.
Remove excess trypsin solution and discard.
Add 100 μL of 25 mM AmBic to each gel slice, ensuring complete coverage.
Incubate samples at 37°C for around 18 h.
Check after 15 min that AmBic still covers the gel slices; add more if necessary.
Prepare fresh peptide extraction buffer (PXB).
Wash new Eppendorf tubes with 100 μL of PXB and label them.
Add 100 μL of PXB to each gel slice.
Incubate samples in PXB for 15 min at 25°C.
Transfer extracted peptides in PXB to appropriately labeled tubes.
Repeat steps for extraction fractions from each gel slice and collect in the same tube.
Dry samples using SpeedVac until completely dried.
Resuspend dried peptide pellet in 100 μL of 0.1% trifluoroacetic acid (TFA) in water.
Purify peptides using Pierce C18 tips to remove salts and detergents.
Dry purified peptides with SpeedVac.
Resuspend peptide pellet with 0.1% formic acid (FA) in water at a concentration of around 500 ng/μL.
Submit samples for LC-MS/MS analysis.
Inject around 1 μg of peptides into the UltiMate 3000 UHPLC system equipped with a C18 analytical LC column.
Load peptides onto a trap C18 column and wash with Mobile phase A at a flow rate of 4 μL/min.

Separate peptides on the analytical C18 column using a step gradient from 4% to 25% Mobile phase B from 10-100 minutes, then from 25% to 45% Mobile phase B from 100-130 minutes, at a flow rate of 300 nL/min and 50°C.
Analyze eluted peptides by high-resolution mass spectrometry in data-dependent acquisition mode (DDA).
Set the survey full scan MS for acquiring in Orbitrap mode with a scan range from m/z 350 to 1800 at a resolution of 120,000.
Select and isolate the most intense parent ions with charge states of 2–6 in 3 s cycles.
Fragment parent ions using higher-energy collisional dissociation (HCD) with 35% normalized collision energy.
Detect fragmented ions at a mass resolution of 30,000 at 200 m/z.
Set the automatic gain control (AGC) target for MS1 to 4 × 10^5 with an ion filling time of 100 ms and for MS2 to 5 × 10^4 with an ion filling time of 60 ms.
Apply dynamic exclusion for 30 s with a 10-ppm mass window.
